h1:
Kaeng Hin Phoeng Rainy-Season Rafting
2 Days, 1 Night
intro: Kaeng Hin Phoeng only opens for rafting during the rainy season, from July through October — the window when the Sai Yai stream runs high and strong enough to push a raft through six back-to-back rapids and actually make it fun. Here's a ready-to-go 2-day, 1-night plan, from checking water levels before you leave and packing right, to booking a rafting crew and the safety checklist that people who've done it say you can't skip.
chips: ⛺ Stay by the Sai Yai stream

blocks.html: Kaeng Hin Phoeng sits inside Khao Yai National Park, on the Saphan Hin side of Na Di district, Prachinburi province. The put-in point for rafting is the Khao Yai Ranger Station 9 (Sai Yai). The draw here is a genuine white-water run you can reach from Bangkok in a single day's drive. But the key thing to understand first: it only opens for rafting during the rainy season, when the water is high enough — outside that season the level drops too low to run. So this trip has to be planned around water levels above all else.

blocks.text: Season and water levels you can actually run

blocks.html: The rafting window at Kaeng Hin Phoeng is July to October, and the stretch when the water is at its best and most fun is usually August to September — which is also when the area holds its annual Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting festival. Before you head out, call to check the water level with the ranger station or the rafting crew you've booked, because the level rises and falls differently from week to week.

items: Too little water (early/late season) — the raft can get stuck on rocks and you'll have to climb out and push in places. Less of a thrill, but safer — good for beginners and older kids.
Just right (Aug–Sep) — lively rapids, bouncy waves, the full rafting experience. This is the most popular time to go.

High/flood water (after heavy back-to-back rain) — muddy water flowing too fast to control. On some days the rangers call off rafting for safety. If you go on a day like this, accept that you might not get on the water at all.

blocks.title: Check before you leave
blocks.html: Call the visitor centre / Ranger Station 9 to ask about the water level at 086-092-6527 or 086-092-6529, ideally 1–2 days before you go. If it rains hard all night, brace for the chance that rafting is temporarily closed the next morning.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Prachinburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Prachinburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: The standard run is the stretch of six rapids back to back, roughly 2.5 kilometres long, rated Grade 3–5 (dropping to 2–3 in lower water). It's a more serious run than a lot of people expect — not a lazy float downstream. The rapids you'll hit, in order:

items: Hin Phoeng Rapid — the first one and the namesake of the place. Strong waves; you'll get soaked right off the bat.
Phak Nam Lom Rapid — a stretch where you paddle on the bow guide's call.
Wang Bon Rapid — a whirlpool on the bend.
Luk Suea Rapid — the one a lot of people say is the wildest.
Wang Sai Rapid — continuous waves.
Hu Hao Rapid — the closing rapid before the take-out point.

blocks.html: The actual rafting is shorter than you'd think — about 30–40 minutes per run. But getting to the put-in means hiking about 2.5 kilometres from the ranger station, around 45 minutes (forest trail, slippery in the rainy season). Most rafting crews carry the rafts and walk you in.

blocks.text: Prices and booking a rafting crew

blocks.html: Price depends on whether you book a private raft or a package with accommodation, and on how many people per raft (an inflatable raft seats about 6–8). The figures below are the range we've seen from local operators — treat them as a rough guide and confirm with the operator when you book.

items.name: Pung Luang Campground Resort
items.blurb: A popular choice for staying right by the rapids. Has a 2-day, 1-night package covering accommodation, two meals, rafting, and transfers — sorted in one place. Good for groups.
items.meta: 2D1N package · about 15 min from the rapids

items.name: Saksupha Resort
items.blurb: Another operator handling both accommodation and rafting packages, with private-raft and activity-inclusive options. Good if you want everything booked through one place.
items.price: ask for pricing by group size

items.name: Private raft, rafting only (local operators)
items.blurb: If you're not staying overnight or already have accommodation, you can book rafting only as a private raft. The price covers the raft, a lead paddler, and safety gear — split per head it gets cheaper with a bigger group.

blocks.title: Why you should book ahead
blocks.html: Rainy-season weekends get very busy, especially Aug–Sep, and rafts are limited. Call to book your crew and accommodation at least 1–2 weeks ahead. Don't count on walking in on the day during a long weekend.

Driving yourself from Bangkok is the easiest — about 3 hours via Kabin Buri district, then on into Na Di toward Saphan Hin and up to Ranger Station 9 (Sai Yai). Without a car, take a BKS bus from Mo Chit 2 to the Kabin Buri bus terminal, then catch a songthaew or hire a ride into the Saphan Hin area.

items: Drive yourself — Bangkok to Kaeng Hin Phoeng, about 3 hrs. The last stretch is the park access road, slippery in the rain, so drive slowly.
Bus + onward ride — Mo Chit 2 → Kabin Buri, then a songthaew into Na Di / Saphan Hin. Leave time for the transfer.
Resort transfer — if you book an all-in package, many operators pick you up from a meeting point. Easiest option if you don't have a car.

blocks.html: Set up at an unhurried pace: stay one night by the water, wake up and raft in the morning when the water's calmer and the crowds are thinner, then head back at your own pace.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Travel, check in, stroll by the stream

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, heading for Kabin Buri / Na Di
items.note: Fill up on fuel and grab snacks for the car — shops are scarce inside the park.

items.activity: Arrive in the Saphan Hin area, check in at your stream-side resort
items.note: Confirm tomorrow's rafting time and meeting point with the crew.
Many resorts have a kitchen doing made-to-order meals.

items.activity: Stroll along the Sai Yai stream, take photos, dip your feet
items.note: See the water level with your own eyes so you know how strong the rapids will be tomorrow.

items.activity: Dinner by the water, early night
items.note: Early start tomorrow — lay out your rafting clothes ahead of time.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Morning rafting, pack up, head home

items.note: Don't stuff yourself — it gets uncomfortable on the hike in to the put-in.

items.activity: Meet the rafting crew, get your life jacket and helmet, listen to the briefing
items.note: Pay attention to the paddle rhythm and hand signals — this part matters more than you'd think.
Trail is slippery in the rain — wear closed-heel shoes that can get wet.

items.activity: Raft the six rapids back to back, ~30–40 min
items.note: Hold the rope, paddle on the bow guide's call, and enjoy it.

items.activity: Take out, shower and change, pack up
items.note: Bring dry clothes and a waterproof bag for the wet stuff.
You can stop at a café or pick up souvenirs around Kabin Buri on the way.

items: Closed-heel shoes that can get wet (strap-back sandals / old sneakers) — no flip-flops, they'll come off for sure.
One set of wet clothes + a spare dry set, packed separately in a waterproof bag.
Camera/phone in a waterproof pouch or on a tether (anything dropped in the water is hard to get back).
Insect repellent, sunscreen, and any personal medication.
Cash — phone signal in the forest can be poor, so bank transfers may not work.

blocks.html: Kaeng Hin Phoeng is a real Grade 3–5 run with waves and rocks under the surface. The fun comes with risk you can manage if you do the following.

items: Wear your life jacket and helmet at all times, strapped tight — don't take them off even when the water is calm.
Listen to the briefing and follow the bow guide — paddle, stop, duck. That's what prevents accidents more than anything.
If you fall in, point your feet downstream and float on your back. Don't try to stand — your foot can get caught between rocks.
No alcohol before rafting, and don't go if you can't swim at all without telling the crew.
Respect the rangers' calls — if the water floods and they call it off that day, accept it. Don't go hunting for an operator who'll take you out anyway.

blocks.title: Who it suits, who should sit out
blocks.html: Very young children, older people with heart or bone conditions, pregnant women, and anyone who can't swim at all should avoid the high-water stretch — or pick a low-water day and tell the crew in advance.

faq.q: What months is Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting open?
faq.a: Only during the rainy season, July through October, with the best and most fun water usually in August–September. Outside that season the level drops too low to run, so call to check the water level with Ranger Station 9 before you travel.

faq.q: How hard is Kaeng Hin Phoeng — is it OK for beginners?
faq.a: It's Grade 3–5, a genuine white-water run, not a lazy float. But there's a lead paddler and a guide on every raft, so beginners can do it if they listen to the briefing and follow the bow guide. Lower water is easier and safer.

faq.q: How much does Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting cost?
faq.a: A private raft for rafting only runs about 2,500–3,500 THB per raft (seats about 6). A 2-day, 1-night package with accommodation, meals, and transfers is around 1,755–2,500 THB per person, depending on group size.

faq.q: Can I raft if I can't swim?
faq.a: To an extent, since you wear a life jacket the whole time — but tell the crew in advance, pick a day when the water isn't strong, and if you're really worried, avoid the flood-water period. Safety before the thrill.

faq.q: Is Kaeng Hin Phoeng far from Bangkok?
faq.a: About a 3-hour drive via Kabin Buri into Na Di and Saphan Hin. Without a car, take a BKS bus from Mo Chit 2 to Kabin Buri, then a songthaew, or use a resort transfer.
